extracted.intended_audience: general readers, comedy writers, and researchers interested in satirical women's media
extracted.subtask_short: writing feminist satire for womens media
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive standards for producing satire that parodies women's magazines and media targeted at women, including headline style, formats (advice columns, listicles, news pieces), and handling sensitive topics. Focuses on the tone, targets, and formats exemplified by the Reductress website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parody the style, tone, and perspective of media targeted towards women
rubrics_metrics.description: Reductress "parodies the style, tone, and perspective of media targeted towards women, especially women's magazines."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emulate the conventions and voice of women's magazines to expose and satirize their assumptions and tropes. Use recognizable magazine structures and rhetorical moves so readers see the target being mocked rather than inventing an unfamiliar register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clickbait-style headlines as a satirical device
rubrics_metrics.description: The site was "conceived as a parody of women's magazines and the clickbait headlines they often employ."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write headlines that mimic clickbait language and urgency to lampoon the attention-grabbing tactics of online women's media. Examples from coverage include headlines like "We're Piercing My Baby's Tongue." Balance exaggeration and plausibility to increase comedic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirize the ways women's media capitalize on feminism while making women feel inadequate
rubrics_metrics.description: The site "gradually expanded its focus to satirizing the ways women's media attempt to capitalize on feminism while still espousing values 'that make [women] feel inadequate.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target hypocrisies where outlets adopt feminist language for clicks or commerce while reinforcing insecurity. Show the contradiction between proclaimed empowerment and practices that produce self-doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parody problematic forms of feminism (e.g., 'white feminism') and lack of privilege awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: The site "has also parodied aspects of feminism, such as white feminism or feminism that lacks awareness of privilege."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique exclusionary or tone-deaf variants of progressive movements by exposing blind spots and privilege. Ensure satire 'punches up' by focusing on power imbalances and complacent actors rather than marginalized people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the formats common to women's media (advice columns, news stories, listicles, confessionals, profiles) and pair with stock photos
rubrics_metrics.description: Reductress "publishes satirical advice columns, news stories, confessionals, listicles, and profiles, paired with a stock photo."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the familiar article formats readers recognize in order to subvert them. Visual pairing (stock photos) reinforces the parody. Vary formats (columns, listicles, profiles) to reach different comedic targets and mimic the magazine ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft headlines that are cutting but sometimes subtle enough to dupe readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage noted the site's "headlines are cutting, but the comedy is sometimes subtle enough to dupe readers" (example cited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a balance between overt satire and plausibility: sharper headlines land immediate laughs, while subtler ones can momentarily fool readers and then reveal the joke, increasing impact. Avoid being so opaque that readers miss the satire or so blunt that nuance is lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: When addressing sensitive topics, confront them with honesty, empathy, and 'punch up' comedic force
rubrics_metrics.description: Particular praise was given for Reductress's 2016 series on rape for being a "powerful reaction" and an example of humor that can 'confront even the most seemingly unseemly topics, so long as it's done with honesty, empathy, and a shit-ton of sagacious fury.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle topics like sexual violence by targeting perpetrators, cultural complacency, and systems (punching up) rather than survivors. Combine sharp critique with empathy and careful framing; satire should illuminate injustice without trivializing trauma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a satirical news-site tone comparable to The Onion
rubrics_metrics.description: The style of its articles "has been compared to that of The Onion."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a deadpan, news-parody voice that treats absurd premises as straight news to heighten irony. Employ faux-objectivity and reportage techniques to amplify comedic contrast between form and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand beyond written pieces into multimedia and live comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Newell and Pappalardo have expressed interest in creating more video content for the site, and Reductress "also hosts a live stand-up comedy show called Haha...WOW."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider video and live performance to extend satire's reach and experiment with timing, tone, and audience interaction. Different media require adapting style and pacing but can reinforce the site's brand and comedic voice.
